events.title: The Fed begins raising its policy target
events.description: The Fed raises its federal funds target by 25 basis points to 1.25%, reporting solid output growth and improved labor markets.

events.title: Microsoft announces a large capital return
events.description: Microsoft announces quarterly dividends, a four-year buyback plan and a special $3 dividend. The special dividend goes ex-dividend November 15 and is paid December 2.

events.title: Apple introduces iPhone
events.description: Apple announces a device combining phone, music player and Internet functions. This is business context, not a guarantee of future shareholder returns.

events.title: The NBER announces a recession
events.description: The NBER identifies December 2007 as the economic peak; the determination is retrospective.

events.title: The Fed moves its target close to zero
events.description: The Fed establishes a 0–0.25% target range amid declining activity and strained credit markets.

what_happened_next.text:
The five years after May 2004 brought a big change. The Federal Reserve raised interest rates as the economy grew. By late 2008, the economy and financial markets were in serious trouble, and the Fed lowered interest rates close to zero. A recession had begun in December 2007, but the official announcement came a year later.

In 2004, Microsoft announced a one-time payment for people who owned its shares and plans to buy some of its own shares back. Apple released the iPhone in 2007. It was a big change for a company then known for computers and music players.

The companies’ results were very different by May 2009. An investment in Apple ended much higher than it started. Microsoft’s ended a little lower, and eBay’s ended much lower. A popular product or familiar company did not promise a winning investment.

The five-year period ended in May 2009, while people were still facing a serious financial crisis. No one could know in May 2004 exactly how the economy or these companies would change.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: The May headlines covered jobs, expensive gas, Iraq, the coming election, cicadas, movies, and sports. Investors were also watching companies such as Apple, Microsoft, and eBay.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The economy went from steady growth to a deep crisis. The companies also made different choices and faced different challenges. What people expected in 2004 could not tell them exactly how each investment would turn out.
reflection.what_faded_away: Election and sports days came and went, and the cicadas appeared for a short time. The financial trouble that came later lasted longer and changed the economy. A busy news story could not tell anyone which investment would do best.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: In May 2004, no one knew when the financial crisis would arrive, how low interest rates would go, whether people would take to the iPhone, or how each company would do. The recession had already begun before its official start date was announced.
